title: SDK Requirements Synthesis: Customer Signals for Multilingual Clients, Auth Patterns, and Streaming Flow Ergonomics
creator: Priya Srinivasan
description: Synthesize incoming customer requests for SDKs and client libraries into a pragmatic, prioritizable requirements set that addresses three linked areas: (1) language coverage (bindings and idiomatic patterns for high-demand languages), (2) authentication and token rotation patterns for enterprise customers (SSO, service accounts, short-lived tokens, KMS integration), and (3) streaming ergonomics (resume semantics, backpressure, reconnect behavior, and developer DX). Goal: deliver a single, defensible prioritization and recommended implementation approach to feed Engineering and Design for Q2 work planning.
acceptance_criteria: Published Confluence synthesis doc that lists incoming customer asks, mapping to themes and a scoring column (customer urgency, ARR risk, engineering effort, maintenance burden, regulatory constraints)
A ranked backlog of SDK requests (top 12) with recommended scope and rough engineering estimate (T-shirt or points)
Design proposals for streaming ergonomics (Node + Python) with example code snippets and migration notes accepted by Design and Engineering
Auth pattern decision documented (primary and fallback) with KMS/HSM considerations and security review sign-off
Three pilot language bindings selected (one new: Go, one matured: Java, one lightweight: Rust) and owners assigned for prototyping in Dedicated/Hosted contexts
notes: Customer signal breakdown: 40% requests for new language bindings (Go, Rust), 35% auth/token rotation and SSO integration, 25% streaming UX and reliability fixes
Scoring rubric candidate: weight = (0.35 * customer_urgency) + (0.30 * revenue_impact) + (0.20 * security_requirements) + (0.15 * engineering_effort_inverted)

Trade-off: strong backward compatibility vs introducing improved streaming primitives. Proposal: keep existing low-level streaming API but add a new 'resumable-session' helper and idiomatic wrappers per language
Engineering preference: centralize token rotation logic in SDK core with a pluggable credential provider interface to allow SSO/service-account integrations without leaking platform internals
Regulatory note: EU enterprise customers requested on-prem token rotation examples; plan to include a short-runbook for Private deployments
